title: Smallest multipliers with leading digit one and a conjecture of Fröhlich (OEIS A190302)
description: theorem A190302: for every n >= 1, the smallest h >= 1 such that the decimal expansion of n*h starts with 1 satisfies 1 <= a(n) < 6. Proves the OEIS conjecture (Felix Frohlich, 2018, verified to n = 10022141) via the exact formula a(n) = 1 if the leading digit of n is 1, else a(n) = ceil(10^(d+1)/n) with d = floor(log10 n); bound ceil(10^(d+1)/(2*10^d)) = 5, sharp since a(2*10^d) = 5. The same bound was asserted without proof by C. R. Greathouse IV (2011) on companion entry A187285 (a(n) is in {n,2n,3n,4n,5n}); this record provides a written proof and a machine-checked formalization - the bound itself is not claimed as new. Standard axioms only; zero sorry, zero native_decide; the featured statement and its dependency closure were additionally re-verified by three independent reimplementations of the Lean 4 kernel (sealed exports deposited on the record). Record-level Apache-2.0 applies to original material only; OEIS verbatim content and %N/%C quotations are redistributed under CC-BY-SA-4.0 (see NOTICE.txt).
